About Seaforge

Seaforge develops offshore data-center vessels engineered to deliver reliable, high-density compute capacity where traditional infrastructure cannot. As global power constraints, interconnection delays, and regulatory friction slow the deployment of new land-based facilities, organizations face increasing difficulty expanding their digital and analytical capabilities.

Seaforge addresses these bottlenecks by shifting critical compute offshore. Each vessel integrates liquid-cooled data halls, onboard power generation, and seawater-based heat rejection, enabling large-scale deployments without dependence on constrained utility grids, freshwater resources, or long permitting cycles.

Built to government-grade security standards and designed for predictable, location-flexible deployment, Seaforge provides a scalable path to expanding national and enterprise compute capacity while reducing environmental impact and improving infrastructure resilience.

results.snippet:
# Ship Data Center Co., Ltd.

Ship Data Center Co., Ltd. is a Maritime Transportation company. ShipDC is a universal platform consisting of rules established in the maritime industry and a data center. It aims to enable the sharing of vessel operational data between stakeholders, the sale of usage rights to shipyards and manufacturers, and many other services without data providers losing profit. The company strives to make data distribution a cooperative domain focusing on competitive domains such as data-driven innovation and the development of new services. Ship Data Center Co., Ltd. employs 2 people (-33.3% YoY, -1 person), founded in 2015. Headquartered in Japan.

## About

Ship Data Center (ShipDC) has been developing a big data platform since 2015 – the Internet of Ships Open Platform (IoS-OP) – for the maritime sector.
The aim of IoS-OP is to create a new maritime sector in the digital age. IoS-OP has two domains; the cooperative domain and the competitive domain. In the cooperative domain, the common rules for data sharing have been developed and the datacenter services for collecting and distributing data from ships are provided. While the cooperative domain allows access to the distributed data, the competitive domain gives opportunities for data driven innovation. Such innovations will lead to new business models and services.

Optimal Transit Unveils Kraaken™: The World’s First Self-Powered Maritime AI Infrastructure Platform with CAPEX & OPEX Costs at a Fraction of Conventional Land-Based Facilities | OptimalTransit

# Optimal Transit Unveils Kraaken™: The World’s First Self-Powered Maritime AI Infrastructure Platform with CAPEX & OPEX Costs at a Fraction of Conventional Land-Based Facilities

Standardized 10 MW to 100 MW offshore AI data centers eliminate dependence on land, the electrical grid, freshwater cooling, and conventional fuel while dramatically reducing infrastructure cost and deployment time.

BEAUFORT, S.C. – July 7, 2026 – Optimal Transit today unveiled Kraaken™, a family of standardized 10 MW, 20 MW, 50 MW and 100 MW self-powered maritime AI data center platforms designed to fundamentally change how hyperscale computing infrastructure is deployed. Artificial intelligence is rapidly becoming constrained by access to electricity, water, land, and permitting. Kraaken™ was designed to remove those constraints.

Unlike conventional AI data centers that depend upon the electrical grid—or dedicated power plants—to satisfy their enormous energy demands, Kraaken™ generates its own continuous electrical power by combining the thermal energy naturally stored in the ocean with waste heat produced by the data center itself.
